THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 15.12.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.61/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE MEMBER-MACT & I ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MANGALURU. D.K.,
AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.7,65,500/- WITH INTEREST @ 9% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed by the insurance company contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive and as such for reducing the compensation this appeal is filed.
2. The factum of accident, death of deceased and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.
Heard the argument of both sides and perused the materials on record.

4. The Tribunal has granted compensation under various heads as follows:
 Sl. Amount in  Particulars M/S Universal Sompo General Insurance ... vs K Mohammed Muneer on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54116746/
2  No.

 2. Towards loss of company 1,00,000/-
3. Towards funeral and other incidental charges 25,000/-
4 Loss of dependency 5,40,000/-
5

Medical expenses 11,500/-
Total 7,76,500/-
5.
The deceased was aged 36 years old, who was wife of claimant No.1 and mother of claimant Nos.2 to 4.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellants that a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
each awarded under the heads 'towards love and affection' and 'towards loss of company', is acceptable.
6. Considering the parameters held by the Tribunal, compensation awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' is found to be on lesser side.

Even towards 'loss of love and affection' and 'loss of company', the compensation awarded is found to be excessive, but by considering the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal, same is found to be just and proper.
8. The claimants have not filed appeal for enhancement.
Therefore, it means the claimants might have satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
When it is found that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is found to be appropriate and proper, the Court does not see any reasons to cause interference with the order passed by the Tribunal.
9. The Tribunal has awarded 9% p.a. interest on the compensation awarded by it, which is scaled down to 6% p.a. and to this extent the appeal is allowed in part.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:2249 ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 15.12.2017 passed by MACT and I Addl.

Senior Civil Judge, Mangaluru, D.K, in MVC No.61/2017 is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to 6% p.a. interest from the date of petition till the date of realization, instead of 9% p.a. interest awarded by the Tribunal.
